question.problem: Let $f(x,y,z) = e^{xy + z},$ where $x = s + t,$ $y = s-t$ and $z = -s^2.$ Calculate $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial t}.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155924/assets/b593a1b60fe8c1aef2c5c229ff426db350e6296b9ecb767494283f0fa3342072.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t), y = y(s,t)$ and $z = z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial t} = \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}\cdot \dfrac{\partial x}{\partial t} + \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}\cdot \dfrac{\partial y}{\partial t} + \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial z}\cdot \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial t}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x, y$ and $z\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y{e}^{xy+z},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x{e}^{xy+z},\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}={e}^{xy+z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =(s-t){e}^{(s+t)(s-t)-{s}^{2}}=(s-t){e}^{-{t}^{2}}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =(s+t){e}^{(s+t)(s-t)-{s}^{2}}=(s+t){e}^{-{t}^{2}}, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & ={e}^{(s+t)(s-t)-{s}^{2}}={e}^{-{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $t,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂t} & =1, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂t} & =-1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂t} & =(s-t){e}^{-{t}^{2}}\cdot 1+(s+t){e}^{-{t}^{2}}\cdot (-1)+{e}^{-{t}^{2}}\cdot 0 \\  & =(s-t-s-t){e}^{-{t}^{2}} \\  & =-2t{e}^{-{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
